editorial:
Imagine waking up to a freezing winter morning in the city and finding a dead dancer lying in the snow. That is how you enter the world of the 87th Precinct. You get to follow a team of detectives who are trying to connect a bunch of weird dots, from a massive showbiz scam to a pile of diamonds and a street drug dealer. The vibe is very gritty and old-school, making you feel like you are right there in the cold streets with the cops. It is not just about one crime, but how different lives collide in a city that does not care if you freeze.

What really works here is how the mystery unfolds without feeling too slow. The acting is solid and the plot keeps you guessing about who is actually pulling the strings. While some of the effects look a bit dated since it is a 90s TV movie, the story holds up great. If you love classic police procedurals, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The detectives finally realize that the murders were part of a cover-up for a huge diamond heist. The killer tried to use the drug world and the showbiz scam as a distraction to hide their tracks. In the final showdown, the police use the evidence from the dead man's vest to trap the culprit. The mystery wraps up with a tense arrest, showing that no matter how clever the scam, the 87th Precinct always finds the truth.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic detective stories and cold-case mysteries.
